scope: compare the client's stored server address with the injected slot address

two_findings.port_byte_order: the port field decodes as 0x2A71 = 10865, while 28970 is 0x712A. The bridge applied socket.htons to a netadr port, but netadr_t.port is host order, so the injected address carries the byte-swapped port. Fixed: the bridge now writes port & 0xFFFF without htons.
two_findings.client_address_zero: the client's stored address at [ebx+0x109260] is all zeros -- it has not been populated. Even with the correct injected port the comparison would fail against a zero address.

next: re-test after the byte-order fix and check whether eax becomes 1 (if the client address is still zero, it will not)
figure out where [ebx+0x109260] is written (probably from the connect response or gamestate) and why it stays zero
that write is likely the same code that fills the server address used by NET_CompareAdr
